NVDA.insight: The expansion with Oracle and Meta arrives alongside revenue that more than doubled YoY: large infrastructure customers are the growth engine. The next test is the 11/17 earnings report.

items.title: Vera Rubin NVL72 at multi-gigawatt scale at Oracle
items.summary: According to Nvidia, Vera Rubin NVL72 and the Vera CPU are generally available on Oracle Cloud (OCI). The expansion of OCI superclusters to multiple gigawatts is an announced plan.

items.title: Expanded partnership with Meta on the Muse models
items.summary: Collaboration aimed at improving inference and training of Meta's Muse model family.

items.title: Vera Rubin platform: from volume production to general availability
items.summary: Presented at the GTC keynote on 03/18/2025, with arrival planned for the second half of 2026 (Nvidia blog). On 05/31/2026 Nvidia said the platform had ramped into volume production, with shipments starting in the fall; on 10/27/2026 the NVL72 became generally available on OCI.

MSFT.insight: Cloud and AI sustain growth while Windows OEM and Xbox decline. The release gives no Copilot figures; the latest metric (30 million seats) is from the previous quarter.

items.title: Azure grows 48% and commercial backlog reaches $677 B
items.summary: Fiscal Q1 2027 release: Azure revenue of $33.2 B; Microsoft Cloud $63.9 B. The CEO highlights security and trust in AI agents as a priority.

items.title: Consumer lines decline
items.summary: Windows OEM and devices revenue fell 22% and Xbox fell 2% in the quarter, according to the same release.

items.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot passes 30 million paid seats
items.summary: Figure disclosed with fiscal Q4 results (July 2026); the previous one was above 20 million, in April.

items.title: Microsoft 365 suite price rises from 07/01/2026; Copilot excluded
items.summary: Announced 12/04/2025: Microsoft 365 E3 goes from $36 to $39 and E5 from $57 to $60 per user/month (Business Standard from $12.50 to $14). Standalone Copilot and Teams SKUs do not change price. Existing customers keep their price until renewal.

items.title: Copilot combines per-user pricing with usage-based billing (Copilot Credits)
items.summary: On 09/25/2026 Microsoft said everyday use stays under the per-user license, and advanced AI (Cowork, Code and Autopilot) moves to usage-based billing with Copilot Credits, which requires the per-user license. The post gives no prices or effective date.

GOOGL.insight: Cloud more than doubled and Gemini became a mass-market product, but capex also more than doubled. EPS came in below expectations: worth checking in the report what separates net income from operating income.

items.title: Gemini 4 "Argon" and "Carbon" at the model frontier
items.summary: The Q3 release cites both models as frontier leaders, with no benchmarks. First-party APIs process about 32 billion tokens per minute, more than 4 times a year earlier.

items.title: Gemini app reaches 1 billion users
items.summary: Described as the fastest-growing product in Google's history. YouTube Music and Premium pass 150 million subscribers.

items.title: Google Cloud: $30.7 B (+103%), helped by TPUs
items.summary: Sales of TPU systems were a "meaningful contributor" to growth. Capital expenditure (capex) rose from $24.0 B to $51.4 B.

items.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite
items.summary: Three new models. Flash Cyber, focused on security, starts in a restricted pilot for governments and partners; 3.6 Flash would use up to 17% fewer tokens.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon available globally
items.summary: Launched on 10/13/2026 in the API (Google AI Studio and the Gemini platform), in Google Antigravity (Ultra subscribers) and in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search (Ultra and Pro subscribers), rolling out gradually.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: restricted access for cyber defenders
items.summary: In the week of 10/28/2026 Google began offering Carbon to a limited group of cyber defenders, expanding gradually through its Fairwind program. There is no date for a broad launch: Google says it is still refining safeguards.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon: introductory API pricing until 11/30/2026
items.summary: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens (cached input 95% off) until 11/30/2026; then it rises to $4 and $20, double. Applies to the public-access version of the model.

META.insight: The strategy combines hardware (AI glasses) with in-house models (Muse) and infrastructure: expanded partnerships with Nvidia (10/26) and AMD (10/27) were announced in the same week.

items.title: Ray-Ban Meta audio glasses, no camera, from $349
items.summary: First glasses in the line built for audio only (the product page says they have no camera). Presented at Connect 2026 on 09/23, with pre-orders from $349 and shipping from 10/13.

items.title: Connect 2026: Meta Adventurer ($249), Muse Charm and Meta VR Glasses
items.summary: Meta Adventurer and Muse Charm: the Connect page gives no price or date (Meta says it will share more later in 2026). The $249 and December figures come from the press. Meta VR Glasses: $1,299.99, spring 2027. Meta expects more than 100 AI glasses styles by the end of 2026.

items.title: Muse, a personal AI agent
items.summary: Launched in the US on 09/08/2026 (iOS, Android and muse.ai), free for most use, with paid plans. On the glasses, Meta said "coming months" at Connect; Meta's help page already describes Muse on the glasses as beta.

items.title: Expanded strategic partnership with AMD
items.summary: AMD's release talks about supporting Meta's "superintelligence" infrastructure; the headline consulted does not detail products.

AMZN.insight: Q3 results come out today (10/29), after this dashboard's data collection. The recent portfolio mixes cloud AI (several models on Bedrock), devices with Alexa+ and ads with agents. The previous quarter's EPS (+216%) probably includes non-operating items.

items.title: New models on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), Claude Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 (Anthropic), Grok 4.7 (xAI), Kimi K3 (Moonshot) and GLM 5.3 (Z.ai) join.

items.title: TorchNeuron, AWS Continuum and AWS Dogwood
items.summary: TorchNeuron runs existing PyTorch code on Trainium chips; Continuum is an AI security service (available); Dogwood is an open-source language to govern agent behavior.

items.title: Alexa+ tablet, kids tablets, redesigned Kindle and Bee wearables
items.summary: The three Alexa Tablets (with Alexa+ built in) and the kids tablets began shipping on 10/14/2026 in the US, Mexico and Canada, and on 10/19 in the UK, Germany, France, Italy and Spain. US prices: $229.99 (8), $329.99 (11) and $499.99 (12 Pro). The lineup also includes a redesigned Kindle and the Bee wearables.

items.title: Amazon Ads Agent and Seller Assistant
items.summary: The 10/29/2026 release cites Amazon Ads Agent, which brings the ad offering into one AI platform, with Full-Funnel Campaigns (sponsored, display, video and TV) available to all US advertisers. In Seller Assistant, new workflows handle restocking and pricing around the clock, and there is a plugin for Amazon Quick and Claude (beta, per Amazon).

AMD.insight: Two fronts show up in the releases: AI racks (Helios) and partnerships with large customers (Meta). The World Labs acquisition (9/28) goes beyond chips; the headline consulted does not detail the thesis. Earnings on 11/03.

items.title: AMD Helios: AI rack in production; OpenAI starts in Q4
items.summary: At Advancing AI 2026 (07/23/2026) AMD said the Helios rack is in production for gigawatt-scale deployment. OpenAI plans to bring it online starting in Q4 2026 and Meta is testing workloads on it. AMD gave no shipping date.

items.title: Expanded strategic partnership with Meta
items.summary: The release is about supporting Meta's "superintelligence" infrastructure.

items.title: Acquisition of World Labs
items.summary: The release announces the purchase to "advance the future of AI computing".

items.title: Instinct MI400 series launched; MI455X is the Helios GPU
items.summary: AMD launched the MI400 series on 07/23/2026; the MI455X is the GPU in the Helios rack, and Anthropic plans up to 2 GW of it. AMD gave no standalone ship date for the MI455X. The MI500 roadmap for 2027 comes from the press and was not checked.

AAPL.insight: The smart-home week (10/13) and the Mac and iPad round (to be confirmed) come before the 11/02 earnings. iPhone details diverged across sources and were therefore left out.

items.title: "Welcome Home" event: HomeView, HomePod mini 2 and Apple TV 4K
items.summary: New 7-inch smart-home display (HomeView), HomePod mini 2, new Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection.

items.title: Mac and iPad round between 10/26 and 10/28
items.summary: The press reports an iPad mini (10/26) and a MacBook Pro and iMac with the M6 chip (10/27), plus a media event on 10/28 with a rumored MacBook Pro with an OLED touch screen. Not confirmed on Apple's site.

CRM.insight: The growth thesis is AI agents (Agentforce, Slackforce, long-horizon agents), with much of it generally available in Oct/Nov. Revenue grows less than that of the other US companies on the list, so monetizing agents is the central point.

items.title: Agentforce Coworker and job-ready agents (Piper, Fin, Hunter)
items.summary: Coworker, an autonomous AI colleague inside Salesforce, is generally available. Ready-made agents for functions such as sales and service; Hunter (outbound sales) arrives in November.

items.title: Slackforce and Claudeforce
items.summary: Brings Salesforce data and workflows to Slack (generally available in October) and to Claude (beta).

items.title: Long-horizon agents and multi-agent orchestration
items.summary: Agents that pursue goals for days or weeks, with human approval points (pilot now, general availability in Nov 2026), and a "super agent" that routes tasks, including to third-party agents.

items.title: Koa, the first CRM reasoning model, and Agent Optimizer
items.summary: Koa is built on Nvidia Nemotron and trained only on synthetic data (pilot). Optimizer finds failure patterns in production sessions (available in October).

items.title: Agentforce: usage-based pricing (Flex Credits) instead of $2 per conversation
items.summary: Salesforce began selling Flex Credits: $0.10 per action (20 credits) and packs of 100,000 credits for $500, alongside the earlier $2-per-conversation model. Enterprise Edition customers and above can get 100,000 credits at no cost.

ORCL.insight: Oracle appears as a large customer of both GPU suppliers: Nvidia (10/27 announcement) and AMD (plan for 50,000 MI450s, from 2025). The official AI World 2026 launch list was not found.

items.title: Vera Rubin NVL72 at multiple gigawatts on OCI
items.summary: According to Nvidia, Vera Rubin NVL72 and the Vera CPU are generally available on Oracle Cloud (OCI). The expansion of OCI superclusters to multiple gigawatts is an announced plan.

items.title: AI World 2026 (10/25 to 10/28): agents and AI in the database
items.summary: The press cites new Fusion AI apps and AI tools for the database, but the articles have no clear date and I found no official event release.

items.title: 50,000 Instinct MI450 GPUs in Helios racks on OCI
items.summary: Plan announced in 2025, with deployment planned from Q3 2026.

00700.HK.insight: AI enters through WeChat and Yuanbao. The company said it will more than double AI investment in 2026, and the quarter's net margin was still around 27%.

items.title: Hunyuan Hy3 integrated into Yuanbao
items.summary: Foundation model with stronger agents (90% task completion rate in internal apps, according to Caixin). It reaches the Yuanbao assistant immediately and the company cut prices for developers.

items.title: WeChat AI agent in beta testing
items.summary: Reported as beta since 6/8/2026, tied to mini programs. General release would depend on regulatory approval; I found no confirmed date.

items.title: AI investment expected to more than double in 2026
items.summary: The company said it expects to more than double spending on Hunyuan, Yuanbao and other AI products this year.

09988.HK.insight: I found no confirmed product announcement in October 2026. EPS came in below expectations and net income fell sharply YoY; the product context (Qwen, Quark) is from 2025. For the causes, the quarter's report is the source.

items.title: Qwen App and Quark AI glasses
items.summary: The Qwen app passed 10 million downloads in its first public-beta week; the Quark glasses run the Qwen model.

items.title: Quark reworked as an AI super assistant
items.summary: Now combines chatbot, deep reasoning and task execution, powered by the Qwen model.

03690.HK.insight: Focus on consumer AI (Xiaomei, Tabbit) and on a merchant platform (CatPaw), with Keeta prioritizing running current markets better. Net income turned positive again in the quarter.

items.title: CatPaw, an agent platform for local merchants
items.summary: AI agent platform aimed at local-service merchants, launched on 7/27.

items.title: Tabbit, an AI-native browser
items.summary: Launched in June 2026. There is also the Xiaomei agent, which takes delivery and ticket orders, tied to Tencent's Yuanbao.

items.title: Keeta: focus on current markets
items.summary: Management prioritizes operations in existing markets and expects the first profitable month in Saudi Arabia before the end of 2026 (an expectation, not a result).

01810.HK.insight: The narrative is in-house chips and electric cars, but the sources I found are from 2025 or are rumors for 2026. In the quarter, revenue fell YoY.

items.title: Successor to the XRING O1 chip planned for 2026
items.summary: An executive confirmed a new chip this year (the name varies across sources: XRING 03 or O2) and the intention of an annual upgrade. No official date.

items.title: YU7 electric SUV and a $28 B R&D plan
items.summary: YU7 SUV presented in May 2025 with sales from July. The company said it will invest about $28 B in core R&D over five years.

09888.HK.insight: The robotaxi (Apollo Go) is the product with the most measurable traction: about 1 million fully driverless rides in Q2 alone. EPS came in below expectations and net income fell sharply.

items.title: Apollo Go passes 23 million cumulative rides
items.summary: About 1 million fully driverless rides in Q2 2026; presence in 27 cities (May 2026).

items.title: International robotaxi expansion
items.summary: Commercial operation in Abu Dhabi, in Dubai (including through Uber) and tests of the 6th generation (RT6) in London, with public service planned for 2027.

items.title: ERNIE 5.0 and new AI chips
items.summary: Multimodal model that understands and generates text, image, audio and video, presented at Baidu World 2025. I found no new model dated 2026.

09618.HK.insight: Bet on robotics and AI for retail and logistics (RMB 10 B through 2028). Quarter revenue was slightly lower YoY.

items.title: RMB 10 B robotics plan through 2028
items.summary: Presented at the World Robot Conference 2026; JD says more than 200 robotics brands already sell in its retail.

items.title: JoyInside: "AI Home" ecosystem
items.summary: Embedded AI platform; the goal is more than 10 million connected devices by the end of 2026. About 100 AI products were presented at 618.

items.title: LangzuTech Packer robotic arm and "Super Brain" LLM in logistics
items.summary: Updated version of the arm for sorting and loading parcels (Q1) and use of Super Brain in more than 1,000 logistics scenarios at 618.

SHOP.insight: Revenue and GMV grow above 30% and AI appears as a new sales channel (AI-originated orders tripled), still small on the base. Net income is well above operating income, which suggests non-operating items: worth checking in the report. Next earnings on 11/03.

items.title: Q2: GMV +32% ($116 B) and revenue +34% ($3.6 B)
items.summary: Free cash flow margin of 18%. For Q3, management projected revenue growth around 30%. Figures come from summaries and earnings-call transcripts.

items.title: Agentic commerce: traffic and orders from AI triple
items.summary: According to the earnings call, traffic and orders from AI channels rose 3x YoY (still a small base). The Universal Commerce Protocol, from early 2026, and the search index of more than 1 billion products support the bet.

items.title: Sidekick: 3.6 times more daily active merchants
items.summary: The AI assistant had about 34 million conversations in the quarter and helped create more than 36,000 custom apps (up from 12,000 in Q1).

items.title: Summer '26 Edition: more than 150 updates
items.summary: New Horizon theme system (10 free themes), POS version 10, an "Agentic" section in the admin showing which AI channels products appear in, and native AI merchandising. Part arrives in phases through Q3.

INTU.insight: Double-digit growth driven by QuickBooks and Credit Karma. The $4.03 EPS is non-GAAP (GAAP was $1.34), the same basis as the estimate, so the surprise is comparable; net income on an accounting basis is well below operating income. The FY27 revenue outlook (+9% to +10%) slows. Next earnings on 11/19.

items.title: Fiscal Q4: revenue +14%, QuickBooks Online Accounting +20%
items.summary: Global Business Solutions (QuickBooks) at $3.4 B (+14%); Credit Karma $743 M (+16%). TurboTax Live grew 37% for the year and is now 53% of TurboTax revenue.

items.title: FY27 outlook: revenue of $23.3 to $23.5 B (+9% to +10%)
items.summary: Non-GAAP EPS projected at $22.88 to $23.12; from FY27, stock-based compensation is included in non-GAAP. Mailchimp becomes a separate segment. The company describes its strategy as an "AI-driven expert platform".

items.title: October QuickBooks update: Intuit Intelligence and Accountant Suite
items.summary: New Intuit Intelligence features in QuickBooks and the Intuit Accountant Suite. QuickBooks Online Accountant will be discontinued in December 2026 (release note from the Canadian site).

items.title: AI-powered construction edition in Intuit Enterprise Suite
items.summary: Also available as a module of QuickBooks Online Advanced.

SPCX.insight: First profit as a public company (IPO on 6/12/2026), with the AI unit (Super Intelligence) surpassing Starlink in revenue for the quarter. The $4.4 B profit comes with stock-compensation expenses from the Cursor acquisition and $19.6 B of capex in the quarter. The $0.35 EPS is diluted GAAP; the press cites consensus and adjusted EPS on different bases.

items.title: Q3: revenue of $14.6 B (+161%) and net income of $4.4 B
items.summary: Super Intelligence (AI) was $7.6 B (+830% YoY), Connectivity (Starlink) $5.2 B (+69%) and Space $1.8 B. Adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 B, according to the release.

items.title: Starlink reaches 13.6 million consumer subscribers
items.summary: Up 1.6 million in the quarter; monthly ARPU of $69 (+5% over the previous quarter). More than 3,800 aircraft with Starlink activated.

items.title: AI compute capacity rises to 1.7 GW (COLOSSUS II)
items.summary: It was 1.4 GW in June and 0.6 GW a year earlier. The release cites new cloud services contracts for third parties and the launch of Grok Bot, an always-on agentic system.

items.title: Completion of the Cursor acquisition (implied value of $60 B)
items.summary: Contributed $608 M of revenue through 9/30. The accounting consideration was $42.5 B, and $23.4 B of stock awards will be recognized over future service.

items.title: Agreement to buy 800 MHz spectrum licenses
items.summary: Starlink Mobile strategy; closing expected in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.
